narrative.h2: Minimalism is the hardest brief to actually pull off

sections.heading: What minimalism really is
sections.body: Minimal video isn't 'less stuff' - it's intentional negative space holding a single subject with rigorous composition. Apple's product films are the benchmark: one object, infinity-curve background, one light direction, micro-movements that reward sustained attention. The traps are obvious only after you fall into them: empty space without compositional rhythm reads as cheap, not refined. The subject has to earn the negative space around it through compositional framing, edge lighting, and motion that's deliberately small.

sections.heading: Where the look comes from
sections.body: Visual canon: Apple's product films (TBWA\Chiat\Day) from the Jony Ive era, Dieter Rams' Braun design photography, Hiroshi Sugimoto's seascapes, Olafur Eliasson's installations at Tate Modern, James Turrell's Skyspace light works, Wes Anderson's symmetrical centering at its minimalist end, Apichatpong Weerasethakul's slow holds in Memoria. Music videos: Sigur Ros' Glosoli directed by Arni & Kinski, Bon Iver's Holocene visualizations, the Erased Tapes label roster (Olafur Arnalds, Nils Frahm). Tunee's minimalist model treats 'minimalist' as compositional restraint, not removed detail - surfaces still need real material response.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Specify the negative-space ratio: 'subject occupies center-third, surrounding 80% empty'. Lock the palette to two values: 'off-white background, single object in matte black'. Name the light direction precisely: 'rim light from camera-left only, no fill'. Add motion language: 'subject rotates 5 degrees, no camera movement'. The temptation is to add 'one more thing' - resist it. Every added element costs the composition more than it adds.
